kurz: [[kakaobutter|Cocoa butter]] can set in several crystal forms. Only one of them gives chocolate its shine and snap.
bild_im_kopf: Like soldiers standing in neat rows (shiny, snaps) or in a wild jumble (dull, crumbly).
was_passiert: As it cools, different fat crystals form. The desired form (form V) only forms in a narrow temperature window. When [[temperieren|tempering]], you melt all crystals, cool so that stable crystals form, and warm slightly to melt the unstable ones again.
warum_wichtig: Explains why chocolate that has melted and set again turns dull and streaky, and why pralines do not shine without tempering.
faustregeln: Dark chocolate: melt to 45–50 °C, cool to about 27 °C, work at 31–32 °C.
Work milk chocolate at 29–30 °C, white at 28–29 °C.
Keep water away: even one drop makes chocolate seize.

stellschrauben.wirkung: one degree too many → crystals melt

skala.name: above this the good crystals melt
